title: Center Register Removal and Installation
introduction:
The center registers are the dashboard’s adjustable air outlets. Getting them out means removing the side trim panel, releasing the center upper trim panel and disconnecting its electrical connector, then reaching the register retainers from behind.

I use the drawings as a map of the hidden catches: blue identifies the part being removed, and magenta highlights the clips or connector release. Think of the register tabs as little door latches around a circle—releasing one does not mean its neighbours have let go.

items.name: Review the applicable precautions
items.detail: Before starting, review the [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and the linked [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184) (100-00 General Information, Description and Operation). This procedure concerns dashboard trim, an electrical connector and air outlets; it does not involve opening refrigerant lines, disconnecting heater water hoses or servicing an electric booster heater.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Disable the remote start feature, if equipped, using the vehicle’s Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before beginning service. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, potentially causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear protective equipment
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling components with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow either precaution may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Trim removal tool
items.detail: Have the trim removal tool depicted in the panel-removal illustrations ready. Use the highlighted clip locations to guide panel release; no tool size or part number is specified.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustrations show a vehicle with center gauges. The procedure is similar on vehicles without center gauges.
edits.why: The gauges identify the illustrated configuration; their absence does not change the stated removal sequence.

edits.text: Use the illustrated trim removal tool to release the instrument panel side trim panel at the marked retaining-clip locations, then remove the panel.
edits.why: The side panel comes off before the larger upper trim panel. I use the highlighted catches to locate its attachments rather than treating the whole edge as a pry point.

edits.text: Release the instrument panel center upper trim panel from the retaining clips marked in the illustration, using the depicted trim removal tool. Ease the panel away far enough to reach its electrical connector, press the highlighted connector release shown in the inset and disconnect the connector. Remove the panel.
edits.why: The upper trim panel carries the center registers. Releasing its mechanical attachments gives access to the connector, which must be disconnected before the panel can come away completely.

edits.text: From the rear of the removed center upper trim panel, release the retaining clips around each center register as illustrated, then remove the registers from the panel.
edits.why: The rear view shows the catches around each register housing. Those catches retain the outlet in the trim panel; the movable airflow louvers are not the retaining clips.

edits.text: Install the parts in reverse removal order: refit the center registers and engage their retaining clips, reconnect the electrical connector and refit the instrument panel center upper trim panel, then refit the instrument panel side trim panel. Check that the clips have re-engaged and the registers and trim panels are seated.
edits.why: Reversing the sequence keeps the connector accessible until it is reconnected and restores each clip attachment before the side trim panel closes the access.
